prompt: Write a one-star review of the Statue of Liberty from a reviewer who is upset that you have to take a boat.
response:
**★☆☆☆☆ — Buyer Beware: It's on an ISLAND**

I don't know who thought this was a good idea, but apparently you can't just walk up to the Statue of Liberty. It's on an island. In the middle of the water. Nobody tells you this until you're standing at the dock watching a boat pull away.

A BOAT. In this day and age. I have to get on a BOAT to look at a statue?

I paid good money expecting to drive up, snap a few photos, and grab a hot dog. Instead I'm told I have to buy a ferry ticket, stand in a line, go through security like I'm boarding a flight to Europe, and then float across the harbor like some kind of pilgrim. The whole thing took HOURS out of my day.

And don't get me started on the water. It was choppy. My stomach was not thrilled. Some guy next to me was filming the skyline like it was the greatest thing he'd ever seen. Sir, we are on a glorified bus that floats.

Would it kill them to build a bridge? A tunnel? A very long escalator? The statue itself is fine, I guess, if you like green ladies holding torches, but the sheer AUDACITY of making me travel by sea knocks this down to one star.

Do better, Lady Liberty. Meet your visitors halfway. On land.
